candidates.title: Reinforcement Learning for Aligning Structure-Based Molecular Generation toward Make-on-Demand Chemical Spaces.
candidates.abstract: Generative models for structure-based drug design have strong potential to accelerate early-stage drug discovery by enabling the conditional generation of target-specific molecules. However, a major bottleneck is that generated compounds are frequently difficult or impossible to synthesize, limiting their direct experimental validation and utility. We address this by optimizing for membership in make-on-demand chemical libraries, ensuring that generated molecules can be directly purchased and tested. To this end, we apply reinforcement learning to a pocket-conditioned generative molecular model, steering generated molecules toward two large make-on-demand spaces: Enamine REAL and Freedom 4.0. We compare an offline, preference-based strategy (direct preference optimization, DPO) and an online RL strategy (DiffusionNFT) across single-target and multi-target settings. In single-target optimization for KRAS, the fraction of unique purchasable candidates rises from 10.0% to 25.5% for Enamine REAL and from 4.3% to 12.1% for Freedom 4.0, while drug-likeness and docking-based affinity proxies are preserved. In multi-target optimization, DPO achieves consistent improvements across diverse protein targets, including a 23-fold increase for the challenging CDK4 pocket. These results demonstrate that RL alignment can substantially improve the experimental accessibility of SBDD candidates without sacrificing structural or chemical quality.

candidates.title: Diffusion-enhanced GFlowNet for solving vehicle routing problems
candidates.abstract: Traditional neural solvers for solving vehicle routing problems (VRPs) often suffer from limited solution diversity, motivating the development of Generative Flow Network (GFlowNet)–based models. However, the effectiveness of these models is frequently constrained by insufficient flow expansion in high-reward regions, limiting their ability to distribute probability across promising solution routes. The deeper exploration could yield superior results. Diffusion models, in contrast, provide stronger structural guidance for exploration. These two paradigms are naturally complementary: GFlowNet can supply edge-level signals for diffusion to embed, while diffusion can guide broader exploration. Leveraging this synergy, we propose Diffusion-Enhanced GFlowNet (DEG), a novel framework that integrates GFlowNet with a diffusion model to encourage richer flow expansion toward highreward regions and derive higher-quality solutions. Specifically, DEG exploits GFlowNet’s inherent diversity to generate edge-specific backward signals, applies the stochastic noise schedule of diffusion to perturb these signals, and then denoises them within the GFlowNet paradigm. To further improve scalability, we introduce a specialized decoder capable of dynamically adapting to diverse problem scales. Extensive experimental evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets, including instances with up to 10,000 nodes, demonstrate that DEG consistently achieves favorable performance compared to baseline methods. The code is available at https://github.com/ZHANG-NI/DEG.

candidates.title: Aligning Molecules and Fragments in a Shared Embedding Space for Property-Aware Fragment Selection.
candidates.abstract: Fragment-based molecular design offers a chemically grounded strategy for exploring drug-like chemical space, yet identifying fragments that are both chemically feasible and relevant to a target property remains challenging. Fragment-level attribution is inherently ambiguous because each molecule contains multiple fragments and the same fragment can occur in molecular contexts with different property values. We introduce Molecule-Fragment Representation Alignment for Generation (M-FRAG), a property-aware framework that aligns molecules and fragments in a shared embedding space. M-FRAG organizes fragments according to their local relationships with parent molecules and their global distribution across molecular properties. Candidate fragments are then prioritized by their distance and distributional proximity to property-relevant molecular regions and used to guide reinforcement-learning-based molecular assembly. Across five docking-based multiobjective optimization tasks, M-FRAG improves the novel hit ratio by up to 58.00% over the strongest locally evaluated primary baseline and achieves the best Novel Top-5% docking scores for all five targets while maintaining strong novelty and chemical validity. These results establish embedding-space-guided fragment selection as an effective and traceable strategy for property-optimized molecular generation.

candidates.title: Degron-Informed Design of DCAF10 Recruiter for Targeted Protein Degradation
authors: Pedro A S Vaz de Castro
candidates.abstract: Targeted protein degradation (TPD) is an emerging biological and therapeutic strategy that harnesses small molecules or biologics to eliminate proteins of interest by engaging the cellular protein degradation machinery. Here, we report DCAF10 as a TPD-competent E3 ligase. Guided by DCAF10's endogenous recognition of N-terminal acetyl-glycine degrons, we developed an Ac-Gly-Phe-Gly (Ac-GFG)-based recruiter capable of inducing DCAF10-dependent degradation of FKBP12 and multiple protein kinases. Interestingly, the Ac-GFG-based recruiter also exhibited a minor dependence on a secondary E3 ligase, FBXO22, potentially due to metabolic conversion that generates a terminal amine-containing species. Structure-activity relationship studies further identified an optimized N-propionyl-Gly-Phe-Ile (Pr-GFI) motif that enables potent degradation of FKBP12 (DC50 = 1.56 nM, Dmax = 96%) with exclusive dependence on DCAF10. We further leveraged this recruiting motif to develop a BRD9 degrader that induces potent, selective, and DCAF10-dependent degradation. Our findings establish the Pr-GFI motif as a potent and selective DCAF10 recruiter and provide a new chemical handle for expanding the scope of TPD.

candidates.title: Predicted templates improve the prediction of antibody-antigen structures by AlphaFold 3 and Boltz-2
candidates.abstract: Motivation: In spite of the much improved protein structure prediction methods, the success rate remains low for antibody-antigen complexes. While this can be improved by computationally demanding massive sampling, results are still much poorer than for most other types of protein-protein interactions. In principle, improvement can be achieved by using templates that are close enough to the native structure of the complex, but these are generally not available for antibody-antigen complexes. Results: We explore the use of templates, generated by the computationally inexpensive rigid body docking program PIPER. Applied to a leakage-free antibody-antigen benchmark set, standard AlphaFold 3 with 1000 random seeds yields acceptable or better models as the top predictions for 56.2% of complexes. Adding the PIPER generated templates in the unmasked version of AlphaFold 3 either increases the success rate to 63.4%, or reaches the same 56.2% success rate in about 200 runs. The template-based approach similarly improves antibody-antigen prediction by Boltz-2. This result demonstrates that the space explored by the ML based approach can be expanded by adding templates prepared by traditional docking, compensating for the lack of evolutionary relationship and the limited availability of training data. Availability and Implementation: The ClusPro server (https://cluspro.bu.edu/login.php) containing the PIPER program is free for non-commercial applications and the program is available by request (https://www.vajdalab.org/). All other study data are included in the article and/or supporting information.

candidates.title: DiffusionOPD: A Unified Perspective of On-Policy Distillation in Diffusion Models
candidates.abstract: Reinforcement learning has emerged as a powerful tool for improving diffusion-based text-to-image models, but existing methods are largely limited to single-task optimization. Extending RL to multiple tasks is challenging: joint optimization suffers from cross-task interference and imbalance, while cascade RL is cumbersome and prone to catastrophic forgetting. We propose DiffusionOPD, a new multi-task training paradigm for diffusion models based on Online Policy Distillation (OPD). DiffusionOPD first trains task-specific teachers independently, then distills their capabilities into a unified student along the student’s own rollout trajectories. This decouples single-task exploration from multi-task integration and avoids the optimization burden of solving all tasks jointly from scratch. Theoretically, we lift the OPD framework from discrete tokens to continuous-state Markov processes, deriving a closed-form per-step KL objective that unifies both stochastic SDE and deterministic ODE refinement via mean-matching. We formally and empirically demonstrate that this analytic gradient provides lower variance and better generality compared to conventional PPO-style policy gradients. Extensive experiments show that DiffusionOPD consistently surpasses both multi-reward RL and cascade RL baselines in training efficiency and final performance, while achieving state-of-the-art results on all evaluated benchmark including DrawBench, OCR, and GenEval.

candidates.title: Comparative Evaluation of Hyperparameter Optimization Strategies for k-Nearest Neighbors over Mixed Domain Search Spaces
candidates.abstract: k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) remains a strong baseline due to its simplicity, interpretability, and non-parametric structure; however, its predictive performance is highly sensitive to interacting hyperparameters. This paper studies search-constrained hyperparameter optimization for KNN over a mixed search space comprising an integer neighborhood size, a categorical distance metric, and a continuous Minkowski exponent. Seven tuning strategies are compared under a unified nested validation protocol with standardized preprocessing: grid search, random search, Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithm, surrogate optimization, particle swarm optimization, and grey wolf optimizer. Experiments on diverse public classification datasets from UCI, OpenML, and Kaggle evaluate predictive performance (accuracy, macro-AUC, cross-entropy), validation loss, and runtime. The results indicate that adaptive optimizers generally provide more favorable performancecost trade-offs than exhaustive grids under limited evaluations, while no single method is uniformly best across all datasets. Rank-based statistical comparisons using non-parametric tests further support the observed differences and motivate practical recommendations for selecting tuning strategies as a function of evaluation search and mixed-domain search-space characteristics.

candidates.title: Latent Class Mixed Model Variational Autoencoders for Scalable Phenotyping of Health Trajectories
candidates.abstract: Clustering longitudinal health trajectories requires handling high-dimensional measurements, irregular visit times, and subject-level heterogeneity while retaining clinically interpretable structure. Existing methods address this only partially: latent-class mixed models yield an interpretable, covariate-driven partition but do not scale past a handful of markers, while deep time-series clustering scales at the cost of that structure and generally requires a common time grid. We introduce the Latent Class Mixed Model Variational Autoencoder (LCMM-VAE), a deep generative model whose latent prior is a mixture of class-specific linear mixed models, so that each subject's latent trajectory decomposes into its class mean trajectory and a subject-specific deviation. We derive a variational EM algorithm whose class responsibilities, random effects and mixed-model parameters are updated in closed form, and provide identifiability guarantees under stated conditions. Experiments on simulated and real longitudinal cohorts show that LCMM-VAE returns a partition, a reconstruction of incomplete trajectories and interpretable class-level dynamics at once, while remaining competitive with classical and deep baselines.

candidates.title: StreamChar: Long-Horizon Streaming Character Audio-Video Generation with Decoupled Orchestration
candidates.abstract: Real-time streaming joint audio-video generation for character animation requires a generator to speak the requested transcript, maintain visual identity across chunks, and run within a strict playback budget. These requirements are difficult to satisfy simultaneously: chunk-wise autoregressive generation can accumulate transcript-audio misalignment and visual drift, while the few-step distillation needed for low latency often degrades spatial diversity and temporal quality. We present StreamChar, a streaming framework that separates long-horizon orchestration from short-window audio-video denoising. An LLM-based orchestrator uses the transcript and historical context to produce frame-aligned audio conditions, and a joint audio-video DiT performs local bidirectional denoising with reference and motion-frame conditioning. For efficient deployment, we use a two-stage distillation pipeline that first compresses the sampler and then fine-tunes the student under online chunk rollouts. A progress-aware pointer aligns partial transcripts with generated audio during rollout training, and a sink-chunk memory provides a persistent visual anchor for reducing long-horizon drift. Experiments on short-clip and long-horizon protocols show that StreamChar runs in real time on a single H100 GPU and provides a favorable system-level trade-off among transcript fidelity, audio-visual synchronization, visual quality, and streaming stability compared with recent joint and audio-driven baselines.

candidates.title: BEACON: Learning Observation-Conditioned Starting Points for Guided Conditional Flow Matching in Microscopy
candidates.abstract: Fluorescence microscopy drives much of modern life science, but accessible imaging setups often yield images degraded by out-of-focus light, limited resolution, and strong signal-dependent noise. Computational restoration can recover high-quality images from such data, enabling cheaper and faster imaging at lower light dose, provided biologically meaningful structures are preserved. Guided conditional flow matching has recently shown strong results for microscopy dehazing and computational super-resolution by learning distributions of plausible restorations. However, it pairs each clean target with an independent standard Gaussian sample, so the starting point of every training path does not leverage the degraded observation. This arbitrary noise--target coupling can produce conflicting velocity targets and makes the conditional velocity field harder to learn. We present BEACON, a $BE$st-of-$K$ $A$daptive learned coupling for guided $CON$ditional flow matching, which learns an observation-conditioned base distribution. During training, a lightweight conditional noise model proposes $K$ starting points for each degraded input, and the candidate with the lowest flow-matching loss supervises both networks, while a KL term keeps the proposal close to the Gaussian prior. At inference, a single draw from the learned proposal is transported along the velocity field, requiring neither candidate selection nor the target. We evaluate BEACON on ten datasets spanning microscopy dehazing and computational super-resolution against 13 baseline families. BEACON achieves the best median perception--distortion rank for every pairing of a fidelity metric (PSNR, MicroMS-SSIM) with a perceptual metric (LPIPS, FID). Code and pretrained models will be released under a permissive license.

candidates.title: SCRIPT: Scalable Diffusion Policy with Multi-stage Training for Language-driven Physics-Based Humanoid Control
candidates.abstract: Controlling physics-based humanoids from natural-language instructions is a critical step toward general-purpose embodied agents. However, existing methods remain constrained by a tension between semantic expressiveness and physical feasibility, often failing to jointly achieve faithful instruction following, high-quality motion, and stable long-horizon control. We propose SCRIPT, a scalable diffusion policy with a multi-stage training framework for language-driven physics-based humanoid control. The core of SCRIPT is a Joint Action-State-Text Diffusion Transformer (JAST-DiT), which represents actions, physical states, and text as dedicated token streams and couples them through joint attention, enabling direct interaction between language semantics and control dynamics. To stabilize autoregressive control, we introduce a nonlinear history conditioning mechanism, which preserves the dense recent context and samples increasingly sparse cues from long-term history. Beyond supervised imitation pre-training, we propose a post-training stage, further improving the performance using Reinforcement Learning with Hybrid Rewards (RLHR). By injecting learnable noise into the flow-sampling process, RLHR effectively improves motion quality and instruction following within closed-loop simulations using hybrid physical feedback and text rewards. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that SCRIPT outperforms prior state-of-the-art methods, with gains across text alignment, motion quality, and physical realism metrics. Furthermore, scaling studies on the 1200-hour MotionMillion dataset demonstrate consistent performance gains with model scaling, highlighting SCRIPT’s robust scalability for large-scale pre-training. Code and data for this paper are available at https://zhanglele12138.github.io/SCRIPT/.

candidates.title: EnSurv: Deep Generative Survival Modeling with Application to Kidney Graft Outcomes
candidates.abstract: Kidney transplantation is the optimal treatment for life-threatening end-stage renal disease, providing significant survival advantages over dialysis. Given the severe shortage of donor organs, accurately predicting the time to premature graft failure is an essential clinical task for optimizing organ allocation and tailoring individualized immunosuppressive therapies. This study is motivated by a comprehensive United Network of Organ Sharing (UNOS) dataset containing 243,443 kidney transplant records with complex multi-region structures and high right-censoring rates. We propose EnSurv (survival engression), a deep generative survival framework designed to capture complex, non-linear clinical covariate interactions for modeling time to graft failure. Within a pre-additive noise model (pre-ANM) family, EnSurv optimizes an energy score augmented with pooled Kaplan-Meier tail completion to handle right-censoring. We identify the pooled-completion target of the objective, establish consistency for its best approximation within the pre-ANM family, and give conditions and error bounds for its relation to true conditional graft survival. EnSurv also provides global explainability through summaries of fitted feature weights and incorporates domain constraints through established clinical directions using a soft gradient penalty. Extensive simulation experiments were conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method in comparison with existing methods. Application to the UNOS cohort demonstrates that EnSurv effectively models individual and region-level effects, consistently outperforming baselines across evaluation metrics encompassing discrimination, calibration, and accuracy.

candidates.title: Adversarial Graph Neural Diffusion for Zero-Day Network Anomaly Detection: A Controlled Evaluation
candidates.abstract: Zero-day intrusions cannot be matched against signatures, so a detector must judge whether a host is behaving abnormally rather than whether it matches a known attack.Continuous-depth graph neural networks that treat message passing as a diffusion process have advanced node classification, and this paper asks whether they transfer to host-level anomaly detection.We present AGND, which combines graph neural diffusion with a time-aware attention operator whose diffusivity decays with the time since two hosts last communicated, and with an adversarial generator that synthesises pseudo-anomalous behaviour.On a controlled benchmark of 1440 windows, 100 hosts and 140 attack episodes from six unseen families, evaluated over 10 independently generated networks, AGND reaches 0.939 AUC-ROC and 0.270 AUC-PR under the original protocol and 0.937 and 0.254 under the corrected protocol of attack-free training and label-free selection.Neither proposed component changes this, and removing the diffusion raises AUC-PR to 0.352 and 0.307 respectively.Isolation forests and one-class support vector machines on the same features exceed every graph model on AUC-PR and a two-layer autoencoder matches the best of them, and the ordering survives training on attack-free windows only, label-free model selection and family-held-out selection.A factorial ablation shows that two hand-engineered relational summaries, not learned graph context, carry the relational signal: without them every method loses between 35 and 60 per cent of its AUC-PR, graph models included.Sweeps of depth, source weight and horizon over all networks show that a single Euler step matches the discrete model, that the loss appears at the second step together with a drop in Dirichlet energy, and that changing the energy through the horizon alone leaves detection quality unchanged, so oversmoothing is part of the mechanism rather than the whole of it.A host-window experiment on CIC-IDS2017 traffic reproduces the absence of a graph advantage but not the diffusion penalty.We report a negative result with a bounded explanation.

candidates.title: Seldon TFM family: Seldon-Mini, Seldon and Seldon+
candidates.abstract: We introduce Seldon, a family of tabular foundation models. Our classifier Seldon+ ranks first among 15 models on TabBench, our benchmark of 124 classification datasets, and on its variant with missing values. In our own runs of public benchmarks, it also ranks first on BeyondArena IID classification and TabBench-Bio, and second on TabArena classification. The open-weight models Seldon-Mini (27M parameters) and Seldon (213M parameters) both lie on the TabArena Pareto front of Elo against inference time: no entry is both more accurate and faster. On TabArena, Seldon ranks fourth and Seldon-Mini seventh among 109 leaderboard entries, and on the IID track of BeyondArena, Seldon ranks second among 42 entries. Seldon-Mini and Seldon handle both classification and regression, use an architecture similar to those of Kumo-Tabular, TabFM and TabPFN-3.5, and are trained on synthetic tables only.

candidates.title: TexSpot: 3D Texture Enhancement with Spatially-uniform Point Latent Representation
candidates.abstract: High-quality 3D textures remain difficult to obtain in current 3D content creation pipelines. Textures produced by 3D generative models often suffer from blurred details, noise and local artifacts, or visible seams introduced by multi-view projection and texture stitching. Effective texture enhancement is closely tied to the underlying texture representation. Existing representations either rely on UV maps, which suffer from distortion and discontinuities during unwrapping, or point-based methods, which tightly couple texture fidelity to geometric density and thus limit efficient high-resolution texture learning. To address these limitations, we introduce TexSpot, a diffusion-based texture enhancement framework. At its core is Texlet, a novel 3D texture representation that merges the geometric expressiveness of point-based 3D textures with the compactness of UV texture maps. Local texture patches are first encoded by a 2D encoder and then aggregated by a 3D encoder to incorporate global shape context, forming Texlet latent vectors. A cascaded 3D-to-2D decoder reconstructs high-quality texture patches from the learned Texlet space. Leveraging this representation, we train a diffusion transformer conditioned on Texlets to refine coarse or imperfect 3D textures by recovering sharper details, suppressing artifacts, and mitigating seam inconsistencies. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TexSpot effectively improves texture fidelity, consistency, and robustness over existing state-of-the-art 3D texture generation and enhancement approaches.

candidates.title: Convoluted Support Matrix Machine in High Dimensions
candidates.abstract: The Support Vector Machine (SVM) has been effective in various discrimination problems.Recently, there has been growing interest in extending the traditional vector-based SVM to accommodate structured matrix inputs.However, the nonsmooth hinge loss poses significant challenges for both theoretical and computational development.To address these issues, we propose a convex smoothing procedure for the hinge loss.Additionally, we introduce an elastic-net type penalty to handle high-dimensional matrix inputs.Our approach surpasses the standard SVM for discrimination involving high-dimensional matrix inputs.The proposed method provably achieves an optimal statistical convergence rate, and the smooth, convex loss function enables the development of a highly efficient optimization algorithm.This algorithm features a fast linear convergence rate and a simple implementation.Extensive simulations and an electroencephalography application demonstrate the method's superiority in classification accuracy and computational efficiency.

candidates.title: Investigation and Optimization of Air Pollution Risk by a Multi-criteria Decision Making Method Using Fuzzy TOPSIS: A Case Study of Construction Workers
candidates.abstract: Background: Investigating human health during work importantly affect the safety and efficiency of the society. Different types of activity, including industrial, constructional, heavy duty ones, etc., affect the health of workers during their activities. In this study, the Multi-Objective Decision-Making (MODM) method was combined with fuzzy TOPSIS to investigate and optimize the air pollution risk affecting the health and safety of construction workers of Lar City, Fars Province, Iran. Methods: The comparison matrices (binary) and the Phillips–Perron test of different criteria and sub-criteria of health risk, including safety view, safety efficiency, understanding the risk, and risk investigation, were assessed to find the most influential factors for the optimization of the health risk of the workers. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. However, among the sub-criteria, the most effective ones were “worker knowledge”, “manager knowledge”, “logistic specialized managers”, “modern facilities”, and “modern technology”. The selection of the linear and non-linear models was conducted according to the F values, and the model parameters were estimated using the Newton-Raphson test. Most coefficients were significant at P= 0.99. The model also has a high describing value of 0.97. The final estimated homogeneity coefficient was equal to 1.31, and it ranged from 0.86 to 2.72 for the critical risk investigation. The significance of the present research is to increase the health and safety of workers during work resulting in a more sustainable and healthier environment. Conclusion: Accordingly, the managers could handle the risks, determine the tolerable risks, indicate the risk of each process to control expenses, and take the essential measures for optimization.

candidates.title: Quaternary adsorption of cadmium(II)/chromium(III)/copper(II)/lead(II) ions from simulated and real wastewater by residual fennel seeds (Foeniculum vulgare) as a removal tool
candidates.abstract: Proper management of wastewater contaminated with heavy metals through biosorption supports climate change mitigation, green growth, and the circular bioeconomy by generating innovative, biodegradable biosorbents. In this study, lignocellulosic materials derived from residual fennel seeds ( Foeniculum vulgare ), in both virgin (FS) and modified (MFS) forms, were employed for the simultaneous adsorption of Cd, Cr, Cu, and Pb ions from simulated and real wastewaters, for the first time. Physicochemical and instrumental characterisations confirmed the presence of diverse functional groups, high cation exchange capacity, and favourable morphology essential for efficient adsorption. The influence of pH, biosorbent mass, initial concentration, and contact time on the adsorption kinetics and capacity was evaluated. Under optimal conditions (solution pH: 5 (FS)/4 (MFS), initial individual analyte concentration: 50 mg/L, contact time: 20 min with 300 mg of biosorbent), maximum adsorption capacities reached 5.1/7.5 (Cr), 6.1/10.2 (Cu), 3.6/6.7 (Cd), and 7.9/14.7 mg/g (Pb) for FS/MFS, with corresponding removal efficiencies of 50-87.5% (FS) and 50-97.5% (MFS). The metal binding affinity followed the order: Cd < Cr < Cu < Pb. Kinetic analysis revealed a strong correlation with the pseudo-second-order and intraparticle diffusion models (average fit of the removal efficiency values: 99.60% (FS) and 99.85% (MFS), with determination coefficients (R2) close to 1). Overall, the developed biosorption process is cost-effective, environmentally benign, and technically applicable, fully aligning with the principles of green chemistry.

candidates.title: GENECraft: A Function- and Prior-Constrained Discrete Dynamical System for Controllable Regulatory DNA Design
candidates.abstract: Designing regulatory DNA requires reconciling two complementary modeling paradigms: genomic language models (gLMs) capture evolutionary syntax without guaranteeing targeted regulatory activity, whereas sequence-to-function predictors provide explicit functional supervision without enforcing native-like sequence plausibility. We introduce GENECraft, a training-free Function- and Prior-Constrained Discrete Dynamical System (FP-DDS) that couples a genomic language model (Carbon) and a functional oracle (AlphaGenome) during inference-time optimization to balance predicted regulatory activity and consistency with genomic sequence priors. GENECraft evolves continuous latent nucleotide logits while evaluating strictly decoded discrete DNA sequences under a time-dependent composite vector field that fuses normalized functional utility, bidirectional contextual prior guidance, and compositional quality penalties, followed by feasibility-first trajectory readout. Across 2,185 loci spanning promoters, multi-constraint enhancers, and 18 transcription factors (TFs), GENECraft achieves full-joint success rates of 62.70%, 65.23%, and 94.56% (macro-averaged), substantially outperforming seven optimization, evolutionary, and generative baselines (which reach at most 2.15% on enhancers). In matched 336-locus ablations, in-loop Carbon guidance reduces native-relative dinucleotide divergence by 7.8--11.5%, enhancer context sensitivity by 10.5%, and TF mutation sensitivity by 11.0%, establishing FP-DDS as a principled framework for controllable regulatory DNA design.

candidates.title: Fast Solution Methods for the Classical 0–1 Knapsack Problem
candidates.abstract: The classical 0--1 knapsack problem is among the simplest integer programs to state and among the most instructive problems for understanding why algorithm selection must follow instance structure. An input contains items with positive integer weights and profits, and the task is to choose a maximum-profit subset whose total weight does not exceed a capacity. The problem is weakly NP-hard, yet many large instances are solved quickly because exact algorithms exploit moderate numeric parameters, strong linear relaxations, dominance relations, or a small set of uncertain variables near the fractional break item. This review develops a theory-guided account of the principal fast solution methods for the classical problem. It proves the correctness and complexity of weight-indexed and profit-indexed dynamic programming, explains sparse Pareto-frontier implementations and reconstruction, derives the fractional-knapsack upper bound used by branch-and-bound methods, and establishes the correctness of meet-in-the-middle search. It then presents the core concept that underlies influential practical solvers and gives a detailed proof of the standard profit-scaling fully polynomial-time approximation scheme. Modern advances based on structured min-plus convolution are placed within this classical landscape rather than treated as isolated results. The central conclusion is that there is no universally fastest knapsack algorithm. Small item counts favor meet-in-the-middle search, moderate capacities or total profits favor dynamic programming, favorable density structure favors core-based exact methods, and very large numeric coefficients favor approximation. A final decision framework translates these theoretical distinctions into an implementable solver-selection policy while identifying open questions concerning adaptivity, certified switching among methods, memory efficiency, and realistic hard-instance generation.

candidates.title: Inference for Delay Differential Equations Using Manifold-Constrained Gaussian Processes
candidates.abstract: Dynamic systems described by differential equations often involve feedback among system components.When there are time delays for components to sense and respond to feedback, delay differential equation (DDE) models are commonly used.This paper considers the problem of inferring unknown system parameters, including the time delays, from noisy and sparse experimental data observed from the system.We propose an extension of manifold-constrained Gaussian processes to conduct parameter inference for DDEs, whereas the time delay parameters have posed a challenge for existing methods that bypass numerical solvers.Our method uses a Bayesian framework to impose a Gaussian process model over the system trajectory, conditioned on the manifold constraint that satisfies the DDEs.For efficient computation, a linear interpolation scheme is developed to approximate the values of the time-delayed system outputs, along with corresponding theoretical error bounds on the approximated derivatives.Two simulation examples, based on Hutchinson's equation and the lac operon system, together with a real-world application using Ontario COVID-19 data,

candidates.title: A multimodal foundation model for tissue proteomics and morphology in cancer
candidates.abstract: Cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment decisions increasingly rely on integrating tissue morphology with specific molecular readouts of the tumor and its microenvironment. H&E histopathology provides scalable morphology, whereas multiplex spatial proteomics quantifies dozens of proteins in situ with spatial context, but remains selectively deployed, often with different marker panels across cohorts. This creates a translational bottleneck: most patients lack high-depth molecular profiling, and existing models rarely integrate morphology and spatial molecular data in a single framework. We present VirTues-M2, a multimodal foundation model that jointly learns from H&E and spatial proteomics using a novel vision transformer-based architecture. By encoding marker identity during pretraining, VirTues-M2 is robust to missing modalities, imperfect modality pairing or registration, and variable marker panels, enabling unified inference for tissue phenotyping, panoptic cell segmentation, virtual staining, annotation-free biomarker discovery, and reinforcement learning-based adaptive marker panel selection to reduce assay burden. As a concrete demonstration of translational utility, in a newly collected cohort of 1,053 treatment-naive non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with paired spatial proteomics and H&E, VirTues-M2 discovers high-risk and low-risk tissue signatures that stratify overall survival in both the discovery cohort and an independent validation cohort, outperforming current state-of-the-art stratification schemes; all enabled by VirTues-M2's ability to jointly analyze both modalities within a single model.

candidates.title: From the ELBO to Maximum Likelihood: Convergence of Variational Autoencoders for Nonlinear Mixed-Effects Modeling
candidates.abstract: Nonlinear mixed-effects (NLME) models are the central statistical models of pharmacometrics, where they support dose selection, individualized dosing and regulatory decisions in drug development. Statistically, NLME modeling is a marginalized likelihood problem. Variational autoencoders (VAEs) solve such problems with a neural network encoder that amortizes the approximation of the intractable posterior distribution, and allow the integration of AI components into NLME modeling. This paper provides the convergence analysis of the VAE-NLME algorithm. First, its version for the evidence lower bound (ELBO) is proven to converge almost surely to the set of stationary points of the ELBO, without assuming that the encoder is trained exactly. Second, the final VAE-NLME algorithm trains the encoder on the ELBO by gradient-based optimization and uses it as proposal for importance-weighted sufficient statistics. It converges almost surely to the set of stationary points of the marginal log-likelihood, without any assumption on the training of the encoder. Thus, it combines the fast gradient-based training of VAEs with the limit of maximum likelihood estimation.

candidates.title: Rayleigh-Quotient-Based Data Classification Method for Machine Learning
candidates.abstract: Inspired by the ability of human ears to distinguish between different kinds of music and the ability of an ancient instrument to play countless beautiful melodies, this paper proposes the Rayleigh-quotient-based data classification method, which implements data classification by selecting an appropriate eigenfunction coordinate system to represent different categories of data and making different categories of data show significant differences in the coordinate components, meanwhile, transforming the selection problem of an eigenfunction coordinate system into a design problem of physical parameters of music instruments, such as designing a non-uniform string or membrane with distributed supports. In theory, the method is based on the eigenvalue problem for Sturm-Liouville differential equation, the eigenvalue problem for functional minimization, and the generalized eigenvalue problem for matrices, which have a time-honored history and can provide strong theoretical foundation and support. In addition, each parameter in the method has a clear physical interpretation and can be adjusted under the guidance of a set of complete theory, and their influence on classification results is definite, avoiding the large time consumption due to randomly adjusting parameters. The data classification procedure is divided into 2 steps, including mass density function design and stiffness function design, which not only simplifies the process of parameter adjustment, but also enables the optimization algorithm to be implemented by the linear programming with a low computational complexity, theoretically guaranteeing a high computational efficiency. Considering the amount of data being classified is large, two kinds of algorithms are developed to implement data classification, where one is a statistical averaging algorithm and the other is an incremental iterative algorithm. Finally, by combining the image database MNIST, the Rayleigh-quotient-based data classification method is employed to build an image classifier, which is trained on the MNIST training set including 60,000 images, and is tested on the MNIST test set including 10,000 images. The classification results show that by selecting an appropriate eigenfunction coordinate system, the Rayleigh quotient distribution of each category of image can be controlled within a very narrow range, while different categories of images show significant difference in the Rayleigh quotient distribution; the classification accuracy on the MNIST training set and on the MNIST test set are stable at about 99.50%, and the maximum accuracy can reach to 100.00% on the MNIST training set and 99.76% on the MNIST test set; and the Rayleigh-quotient threshold can be selected within a very wide range, beneficial for the robustness and stability of data classification.

candidates.title: OmniHarness-RSI: Modality-Aware Harness Evolution for Omnimodal Understanding
candidates.abstract: Recent advances in harness-based recursive self-improvement (RSI) have improved video understanding by evolving executable agent workflows without updating foundation model parameters. However, extending this paradigm to omnimodal understanding remains challenging, as the heterogeneous and interdependent nature of multimodal perception and reasoning creates a complex evolution space, making targeted harness optimization difficult. To address these challenges, we propose OmniHarness-RSI, a modality-aware framework for evolving agent harnesses. Specifically, we factorize the evolution space into three capability dimensions: modality routing and collaboration, modality-aware evidence localization, and modality-specific perception. Based on this factorization, we construct a Factorized-Harness Agent integrating specialized perception experts and audio-video retrieval tools. We further introduce modality-guided harness evolution, which identifies deficiencies through structured modality-capability attribution and refines corresponding harness strategies through interactive code revisions and execution feedback. Validation-guided selection and held-out evaluation assess generalization within and across datasets. Experiments on WorldSense, Daily-Omni, and OmniVideoBench demonstrate test accuracy improvements of 8.86, 8.13, and 6.23 percentage points, respectively, consistently outperforming modality-agnostic RSI. The evolved harnesses also demonstrate cross-dataset transfer without adaptation, while reducing planner calls and viewed frames.

candidates.title: Nasal in-situ Transferosomes as a Platform Technology for Nose-to-Brain Drug Delivery
candidates.abstract: The blood-brain barrier (BBB) represents a major obstacle in the therapeutic management of disorders related to the central nervous system (CNS), blocking the access of almost 98% of small molecule medications and practically all large molecules. Intranasal drug administration represents a viable alternative to overcome the BBB, based on its ability to deliver directly from the nasal cavities into the brain using the routes of olfactory and trigeminal nerves, offering a direct nose-to-brain drug delivery pathway. Despite its advantages, intranasal drug delivery remains constrained by factors such as quick clearance, short retention and poor permeation of the drugs through biological membranes, to address these challenges, the in-situ gelling systems containing mucoadhesive polymers have been developed. Nasal in-situ transferosomal gels offer a novel formulation technique that incorporates the benefits of both transferosomal vesicular drug delivery systems and stimuli-responsive gel matrices for brain targeting. Keywords: Transferosomes, in-situ gel, Intranasal, Nose-to-brain, Blood-brain barrier, Vesicular drug delivery, Mucoadhesive systems, Brain targeting.

candidates.title: Functional hot-spots and communication networks of the cellular prion protein from information-theoretical measures
candidates.abstract: The cellular prion protein (PrPC) is a ~33 kDa molecule featuring a disordered region and a globular part, mostly expressed in the brain and in the central nervous system. The biological role of this protein is still unclear, but its pathogenic behavior in specific conditions has been ascertained. In fact, for reasons that are still under scrutiny, PrPC may convert to its misfolded counterpart PrPSc, which accumulates in tissues and gives rise to a plethora of neurodegenerative diseases. At this day, the mechanism underlying the misfolding process of PrPC to PrPSc is not fully understood. Here, we analyze molecular dynamics simulations of PrPC by means of information-theoretical approaches to single out specific residues that might play a key functional role in the protein, and to identify the network of communication that relays mechanical signals among distal regions of the molecule. We found such hot-spots in the alpha-I helix and the beta-II--alpha-II hinge, which are involved in the initiation of the misfolding process; furthermore, the pair Val209-Cys214 acts as the main link for the information relay between the two aforementioned regions. These observations suggest that the main determinants that trigger the pathogenic conformational transition of PrPC's globular domain are inherently encoded in its structure; this result opens the possibility of developing therapeutic molecules that interfere with these functional elements to mitigate the protein's misfolding and aggregation.

candidates.title: Emerging Role of Artificial Intelligence in Pharmaceutical QC and QA and its Applications across the Industry
candidates.abstract: Quality Control (QC) and Quality Assurance (QA) are key elements in the pharmaceutical sector. They help to ensure the safety, efficacy and consistency of medicines. This article discusses the purpose of QC and QA for pharmaceutical manufacturing in the modern era and outlines their development, principles and problems relating to the application of technology and universal quality standards. The article reaffirms the need for continuous and seamless improvement in the maintenance of quality system improvements that are responsible for global health standards and that can be applied to licensed drugs in a wide range of settings, ensuring the effectiveness of medicines delivered to patients in a sustainable manner. QC and QA are important components in pharmaceutical production. Their combined function is to ensure that all products are safe, efficient and reliable. As the industry evolves and moves toward digitalization, automation and data-centric systems, QC and QA evolve from reactive functions to predictive and preventive tools. Continuous improvements, regulatory compliance and the adoption of technology will shape the future of pharmaceutical quality. This paper also analyzes the beneficial use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) within the pharmaceutical sector throughout all phases, from drug discovery to drug development, as well as in various departments. Besides necessitating less human labor, it also improves the efficacy of clinical research and pharmaceutical output while diminishing the likelihood of mistake. The report examines the existing challenges in the implementation of AI within the pharmaceutical sector. Furthermore, it evaluates existing challenges and proposes remedies.

candidates.title: Next-generation multispecific antibodies for oncology: mechanisms and clinical translation
candidates.abstract: Monoclonal antibodies are central to modern targeted cancer therapy and immunotherapy. However, clonal heterogeneity and dynamic changes in the tumor microenvironment can enable solid tumors to evade single-target therapies. Multispecific antibodies offer a strategy to address these limitations by integrating distinct binding specificities within a single molecule. Yet neither increasing the number of targets nor increasing binding affinity alone guarantees clinical benefit. A central challenge is to coordinate immune-cell redirection, conditional activation, and Boolean logic gating with precise spatial and temporal control. These capabilities must be achieved while ensuring molecular developability, meeting chemistry, manufacturing, and controls requirements, and maintaining an adequate therapeutic window. Using intended biological function as the organizing principle, this Review examines how molecular architecture, affinity engineering, Fc-region engineering, and logic-gated design shape pharmacological profiles and clinical safety. We also discuss the implications of internalization kinetics for bispecific antibody-drug conjugates. We then examine mechanisms of therapeutic resistance and immune-niche remodeling within the tumor microenvironment and assess progress in clinical translation. Particular attention is given to the fidelity of preclinical models, biomarker limitations, strategies to widen the therapeutic window, and combination and sequential treatment regimens. Finally, we discuss emerging directions, including logic-gated activation, in situ immune priming with oncolytic viruses or vaccines, and artificial intelligence-guided antibody design. Together, these perspectives provide a framework for aligning molecular design with biological context and translational requirements to guide the development of next-generation multispecific cancer therapeutics.

candidates.title: From Safety-Driven Redundancy to Value-Driven Architecture: An ODD-Based Rationalization Framework for Level 4 Autonomous Vehicles
candidates.abstract: Level 4 autonomous vehicles require fault-tolerant architectures that preserve critical driving functions under sensing, computing, communication, power, and actuation failures. As these systems progress toward industrial scalability, architectural complexity, validation burden, integration effort, and lifecycle cost become increasingly relevant. This study proposes an Operational Design Domain (ODD)-based, safety-constrained systems-engineering framework for architecture rationalization. ODD-specific capabilities, physical fault assumptions, post-fault operational policies, and spatial sensing requirements are propagated through an integrated safety-feasibility gate. Architecture transformations, including removal, relocation, functional reassignment, and consolidation, are evaluated only within the resulting safety-feasible design space, followed by lifecycle-cost sensitivity and robust multiobjective Pareto analysis. A generic, synthetically parameterized Level 4 architecture is used as a demonstrative computational case study. Within this modeled design space, direct ablation showed limited rationalization potential, whereas directional redistribution and functional consolidation generated a broader set of safety-feasible candidates. Under the illustrative lifecycle-cost model, the best nominal candidate achieved a 5.55% normalized cost reduction and remained cost-reducing across all 5,000 sampled points in the prescribed uncertainty domain. The analysis identified 15 non-dominated architecture-policy solutions representing seven physical transformations. The results support capability-based, policy-conditioned, and lifecycle-aware architecture rationalization under the stated assumptions, with safety retained as a non-compensatory feasibility constraint. The reported transformations are design candidates rather than validated production architectures.
